title: Branch Travel Cost Calculator: Visit Costs
description: Cost out travel between branches with the Branch Travel Cost Calculator — mileage, rate and trip totals a manager can approve. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a rep's 214-mile round of branch visits at an example reimbursement rate of $0.67 per mile comes to $143.38 — before parking and tolls join the claim.
quick_answer: The Branch Travel Cost Calculator totals what a trip between your company's branches actually costs: distance multiplied by your mileage rate, with trip costs on top. Enter the journey and the rate your policy pays, and read a defensible total for expense claims and visit planning.

faq: The cost of branch-to-branch travel: journey distance × your mileage rate, with the trip's other costs added as you enter them — a claim-ready total.
Yes. Enter the trip, read the total, claim it.
As accurate as its inputs: the measured distance and your policy's current rate. The arithmetic is exact; the rate is your employer's to set.
Is the mileage rate a tax rate?
Only if your policy uses one. Many employers reimburse at a standard government-published rate and many use their own — enter whichever your policy names.
Can it handle several branches in one trip?
Total the day's legs into one distance and cost that — a round of visits is one journey for claim purposes.
No — cost follows distance and rates, not traffic. Traffic changes the time (see the ETA Calculator), rarely the mileage.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind, detour and respect geography. Claims must use the road figure — it is the distance actually travelled and reimbursed.
Should mileage be claimed per leg or per day?
Per day is the usual claim unit — the day's legs summed. The calculator prices the day; your policy decides the paperwork shape.
What about the drive home from the last branch?
It is part of the journey. Measure the full round, not just the inter-branch legs — the return is travelled and reimbursed like the rest.
